newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Arthur Barnett half yr sales fall sharply.
newsitem.headline: Arthur Barnett half yr sales fall sharply.

text.p: Retailer Arthur Barnett Ltd said on Thursday that sales for the half year to February 1 fell to NZ$15.06 million from $24.41 million in the previous corresponding period.
The company reported an unaudited net profit for the six months of $197,000, compared with $816,000 for the same period last year. No tax was payable.
Arthur Barnett said the fall in sales reflected the closure of its Alexandra store, and a conscious decision to rationalise the mix of its department stores in Christchurch, Dunedin and Balclutha.
This rationalisation came particularly in some categories of low margin big ticket items, including floor coverings, some furniture ranges and home appliances.

"The complete demolition and reconstruction of our flagship department store in the new Meridian development in Dunedin severely reduced our trading capabilities and that disruption will continue until the entire shopping complex opens in September," the company said.
"In addition to this disruption, retail spending market-wide was considerably down on previous years."

The company announced an unimputed interim dividend of three cents per share on ordinary shares. In addition, new ordinary shares will be paid an unimputed dividend of 0.83 cents per share. -- Wellington Newsroom (64 4) 4734746
